query: What signals suggest an expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the asset from short_description/ci into interpretable buckets, giving a genuine axis to compare decline rates by asset type. Sample values (service_subscription for ISP Services, hardware_device for Dell Laptop, miscellaneous for hardware component) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: asset_creation_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Whether an asset was manually created vs auto-generated is not derivable from the provided source text (short_description, ci, processed_date). All samples are labeled 'manually_created' with no textual warrant, suggesting an unsupported/near-invented assertion. Also weak analytical leverage for a decline query.

per_column.name: department_classification
per_column.rationale: The original table already has a 'department' column, so this is largely redundant. Worse, the sample values appear unsupported by the source text: 'Provision of Services for iPod touch' -> 'sales' and a hardware component -> 'sales' have no textual basis, indicating invented specifics.

per_column.name: travel_asset_flag
per_column.rationale: A travel-related flag could plausibly correlate with expense declines, offering a modest new axis. Samples are all 'False' and consistent with non-travel descriptions, so groundedness is reasonable though it overlaps conceptually with asset_category_type's travel_equipment bucket.

per_column.name: requester_repeat_status
per_column.rationale: Requester frequency is a genuinely useful signal for predicting declines. However it requires aggregating across the 'user' column, and the sample assignments (same-looking single rows labeled 'single_request' vs 'high_frequency_user') are not verifiable from the per-row source text shown, and no user field is provided in the samples, raising grounding concerns.

per_column.name: source_tracking_present
per_column.rationale: Essentially a presence flag largely restating whether source_id/tracking exists; low analytical leverage and close to a trivial has-field indicator. Values are plausibly derivable from field presence but the mapping is opaque.

judge.rationale: The set offers a couple of genuinely useful axes (asset_category_type, requester_repeat_status, travel flag) for reasoning about declines, but several columns are weak: department_classification is redundant with the existing 'department' column and its sample values appear invented, asset_creation_mechanism asserts a manual/auto distinction with no textual support, and source_tracking_present is close to a trivial presence flag. Multiple columns show values not clearly derivable from the provided source text, lowering overall groundedness.
